$comment: Source of truth for the Agent Bridge design language (docs/design/ui.md). Generated outputs (XAML ThemeDictionaries, CSS custom properties, later SwiftUI and Compose) come from this file; never hand-edit a generated copy. Colours are sRGB hex or rgba(). 'hc' maps a role to a system colour name for high contrast.

bridge.use: primary actions, selection, focus, the mark, the 'new activity' dot

needs.use: a question or approval is waiting

active.use: working and delegating glyphs only; never a control

agent.use: driven by an agent (#46), and nothing else

external.use: a collaborator's session or an external agent (#519): always beside the outlined diamond, the word External or a verified @login; never Needs you, a count, a count badge or a notification

accent.$comment: WinUI's accent palette (SystemAccentColor and its Light1-3/Dark1-3 shades), so the controls that follow the system accent (accent buttons, the selection pill, checked radio buttons, checkboxes and toggles, a focused field's edge, selected text, hyperlinks) take Bridge rather than the person's Windows accent (#180). Theme-agnostic, as Windows' own palette is: dark-theme controls fill with light2 and set link text in light3, light-theme ones fill with dark1 and set link text in dark2, and interaction states are those fills at reduced opacity. light2 is bridge.dark and dark1 is bridge.light, taken from the role, so only the shades around them are here. High contrast ignores the palette: WinUI uses system colours there.

winuiText.$comment: Not set, only measured: WinUI's own text on an accent fill (TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary) in each theme, and selected text on SystemAccentColor (TextOnAccentFillColorSelectedText).

hyperlink.$comment: Hyperlinks in text: words in Bridge (ui.md §3), lighter (dark theme) or darker (light theme) under the pointer, and darker again pressed in light. light1 is 4.15:1 on the dark needs fill, too faint for a link in a question, so a dark-theme press stays Bridge. Shade names from accent.windows, or 'bridge' for the role; high contrast is the system's Hotlight.

hcVariants.$comment: High contrast for a role's variants, by the variant's prefix: 'role' is the role's own hc. 'on' is text on the role's fill, 'ink' the '!' on the needs disc.
hcVariants.head: role

rules: Status colours are never used on controls; controls use bridge.
Secondary and tertiary text are the primary text colour at reduced opacity (see surface.*.text2/text3), never a separate grey.
Every role reaches 3:1 against its surface as a graphic; any text in a role colour reaches 4.5:1.

contrast.$comment: What tools/design-gen's tests hold the Windows/PWA surfaces to, in dark and light (ui.md §3, §9). Every role is a graphic on every surface and on every role's fill* (the question card). Text is surface text/text2/text3, every role's text* and head* variant, and the roles in roleText, which clients may set words in, each on every surface and every fill* except as notOnFills says; on* is text on the role itself. A role not in roleText is words only through its text variant: active is never words (4.46:1 on the dark card), and danger's words are danger.text (#FF6B6B is 3.72:1 on the dark needs fill). text3 is 4.30:1 on the dark needs fill, so it is not used there. ink* is a graphic on its role. Translucent tokens are measured composited over the surface. The hyperlink brushes (color.accent.hyperlink) are text everywhere text is, and WinUI's own words on the accent palette (color.accent.winuiText) are measured on it.

tints.$comment: A tint over a surface (inline code, a code block, a read-only field, a machine row, a badge) and the only words that may sit on it, each measured on the tint over each surface in over. Never a tint on a role fill: light bridge is 4.41:1 on subtle over the needs fill, so code in a question takes the card colour.

windows.note: On WinUI use Mica for the shell and LayerFillColorDefault for the layer where available; these values are the fallback and the PWA's. In high contrast every surface is the system Window and every line and text WindowText, so selection shows by its bridge accent, not its fill.

macos.note: Use NSVisualEffectView sidebar material; these values approximate it for mock-ups and tests.

ios.note: text2 light is darker than UIKit's secondaryLabel (0.60) so it meets 4.5:1; use semantic system colours for everything else.

android.note: Material 3 scheme seeded from bridge. Dynamic colour may restyle surfaces but never status roles.

sans.note: Our own OFL font, a tuned Inter (see design/fonts/slipgates-sans/README.md, #544), for every piece of text that isn't mono. Bundle it in every client: hinted statics in one collection on Windows, the variable pair everywhere else. The rest of the stack is the fallback while it loads or where it lacks a glyph.

mono.note: Our own OFL font, a modified Iosevka (see design/fonts/slipgates-mono/README.md). Bundle it in every client; the rest of the stack is the fallback while it loads or where it lacks a glyph.

type.synthesis: none: every weight and style the ramps and inline styles use is a real face of the bundled family, and no client lets the platform fake one (ui.md §4.2, #544). The generator refuses a weight or style the font files lack.
type.numerals: tabular everywhere a number can change (times, counts, percentages, durations)

tracking.$comment: Letter-spacing in em (docs/design/ui.md §4.3, #544 §11): +2% on the title role on every platform, whatever weight the platform sets it at, and on the wordmark, so they don't read condensed. Every other role, body text above all, stays untracked: 0 is the default and the generator refuses tracking on row, reading, meta or code. Emitted as CSS letter-spacing, WinUI CharacterSpacing (thousandths of an em), Apple tracking (em times the point size) and Android letterSpacing (em).

type.readingMeasure: about 68 characters (max-width 735-770 px on desktop: Slipgates Sans sets about 8% wider than Segoe UI Variable, #544)

inlineMono.$comment: Mono inline with the text face (docs/design/ui.md §4.2, #215): scaled so its x-height matches the text face's, at the same weight, baseline and line height. Each xHeight is the face's OS/2 sxHeight in its unitsPerEm; tools/design-gen's tests measure both from the bundled files. Every platform's text face is now Slipgates Sans; the platforms stay listed so a platform may yet differ. The generator emits, per platform, the text face's ratio (for CSS font-size-adjust) and the scale mono takes (text / mono), and per ramp role on Windows the inline mono size, never under minSize.

rules: 24 between blocks in the conversation; 8 between a speaker label and its text.
Panes pad 20-24 on desktop, 16-20 on phones.
A status glyph aligns with the first line of its row's text, not the row's centre.

layout.twoPane: list 264-320 · session with Conversation / Delegates / Tools tabs
layout.onePane: push navigation: list → session → delegate (sheet on phones)

windows.$comment: The Windows app's sizes in px (ui.md §5.2, §7): the title bar, the smallest window, the list and inspector panes (each by default, and the narrowest and widest a divider takes it, #297), the narrowest the session pane gives way to them, the dividers' grip and the line they draw while pointed at, dragged or focused, the reading measure, and the longest a machine tab's name is drawn before it is cut short (ui.md §6.1, #290).

motion.$comment: docs/design/ui.md §5.3. Durations in ms, easings as cubic-bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2], distances in px (epx on Windows, pt on Apple, dp on Android). Nothing but the glyphs runs longer than limitMs, and no easing leaves 0-1 on y (no overshoot). A platform's own transitions (a WinUI theme transition, UIKit's push and sheets, Material's) keep the platform's timing; these time what a client draws itself.

working.what: the arc turns once per period

delegating.what: the satellites drift, one orbit per period

windows.source: WinUI's ControlFasterAnimationDuration, ControlFastAnimationDuration and ControlNormalAnimationDuration; Fluent's Fast Out Slow In and Slow Out Fast In, and Fluent 2's easy ease

apple.source: SwiftUI: springs with no bounce for movement, and the system's easeInOut, easeOut and easeIn for fades

spring.$comment: Spring(response:dampingFraction:). response is in seconds; a damping fraction of 1 settles without overshoot.

android.source: Material 3: short2, short4 and medium2; standard, standard decelerate and standard accelerate

catalogue.$comment: One entry per row of ui.md §5.3's table. duration and easing time the entry (or the move); exit times the leaving half; distance is how far it travels, when that is a token. reduced is its form under reduced motion: crossFade (no travel, the crossFade duration) or instant.

appIcon.$comment: The app icon (ui.md §7, App icon; design/README.md): design/icons/mark.svg on a plate, in each platform's container. One icon in every theme: the plate is always dark, so the mark is the Bridge role's dark value. edge is a hairline inside the plate, so the tile still shows on a dark taskbar. Each container has its own grid (the board's or the platform template's units): plate is the plate's side, centred, radius its corners, edge the hairline's width, and mark the side of the mark's 48 box, centred. tools/design-gen draws design/app-icon/*.svg and every client's rasters from these.

windows.use: Windows tile: the app's .ico above windowsSmall's sizes, its toast logo, and the PWA's favicon and manifest 'any' icons

windowsSmall.use: Windows tile at 24 px and under, where the full tile's ring would be thinner than a pixel: less margin, no edge

macos.use: macOS rounded square on Apple's 1024 grid; the drop shadow is the asset catalog's (P5)

ios.use: iOS: full bleed and opaque, masked to the squircle by the system; the PWA's apple-touch-icon

android.use: Android adaptive icon on the 108 dp grid: the plate is the background layer, the mark the foreground and monochrome layers; the launcher's mask shows the central 72

maskable.use: The PWA's maskable icons: full bleed, the mark inside the central 80% safe zone at Android's proportion
